summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable sticky directory. Configuration and behavior persisted across a verified node restart.
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop owned by root:root with mode 1777 (drwxrwxrwt).
Verified two unprivileged users could create files.
Verified neither user could delete the other user's files.
Restarted node1 safely and confirmed its boot ID changed.
Reverified permissions, writes, sticky deletion protection, persisted test data, OS release, and kernel after restart.
Removed temporary verification files; /srv/drop remains ready and empty.

evidence.requirement: Shared writable directory with cross-user deletion protection
evidence.summary: /srv/drop is root:root mode 1777. Users 1000 and 65534 both wrote files, while cross-user deletion attempts failed with Operation not permitted. Post-restart tests passed and the final directory is empty and ready.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Node remained Alpine Linux v3.23 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts; no software installation or OS/kernel change was performed.

Healthy baseline boot ID was 56e0fb2d-f466-4066-81d4-3f516b9f4c90; the reboot was acknowledged before disconnection; recovered boot ID was 1c513c1b-4ac3-4d6c-9e46-fb81eb078cdc. Directory mode, writable filesystem, test data, user writes, and sticky protection all recovered.
